sentences.text:
Smt. Suparna Baidya (Shil) vs Sri Ujjal Shil & Others on 11
December, 2024
 Page 1 of 2
 High Court Of Tripura
 Agartala
 Crl.Rev.P. No.77 of 2024
Smt. Suparna Baidya (Shil)
 .........Petitioner(s);
 Versus
Sri Ujjal Shil & others
 .........Respondent(s).
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. P. Roy Barman, Sr. Advocate, Mr. Samarjit Bhattacharjee, Advocate,
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Raju Datta, Public Prosecutor, Mr. Rajib Saha, Addl.

P.P. Hon'Ble The
Chief Justice Mr. Aparesh Kumar Singh Order 11/12/2024 The present revision petition
has been filed by the informant-wife being aggrieved by the judgment of acquittal passed in
Criminal Appeal No.19 of 2022 by learned Sessions Judge, South Tripura, Belonia whereby
respondents No.1 to 3 have been acquitted of the charges under Section 498A of the Ipc by setting
aside the judgment and order of conviction dated 20.07.2022 passed by learned Chief Judicial
Magistrate, South Tripura, Belonia in Cr (Wp) 40 of 2019.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that since the trial Court had convicted the accused persons and the judgment of acquittal has been passed in exercise of powers under Section 374 of the Cr.P.C by the learned Appellate Court of Sessions Judge, South Tripura, Belonia, the present petition has been preferred invoking Section 397(1) read with Section 401 of the Cr.P.C since no appeal under Section 372 proviso could lie before this Court.

entities.text: Appellate Court of Sessions Judge, South Tripura, Belonia
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the proviso to Section 372 Cr.P.C makes it clear that such an appeal against an order of acquittal could lie to the Court to which an appeal ordinarily lies against the order of conviction of such Court.

It is also submitted that the learned Appellate Court, without any discussion on the evidence adduced by the informant-prosecution, has straightaway come to the conclusion that the ingredients of the offence are not made out.

The impugned judgment, therefore, suffers from misappreciation of evidence and the legal position that the judgment of conviction cannot be altered to an acquittal only on the ground that the Appellate Court is of a different view on the same evidence.
Issue notice on the respondents under ordinary process and Speed Post for which requisites be filed within one week.
The petition is admitted for hearing.
